label: ssec:descent
html:
The descent machinery connects the infinite brane tower to finite-dimensional geometry. Given a quantum observable universe (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) with brane tower \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} (recursive brane tower), the descent lemma (descent lemma) shows that restriction down the tower is split by the ascent and, for A = \mathcal{O}(G), is a Hopf map, and that the induced descent map on endomorphisms is a surjective, equivariant algebra homomorphism on the block-diagonal subalgebra. Only the base level A_0 = A carries the full QOU structure. The descent involution (descent involution) then splits each A_n into eigenspaces whose direct limit recovers the physical algebra. One now develops this descent involution, its eigenspace decomposition, and the resulting mass-decomposition formula.

This arc proceeds in three steps. One first verifies the existence and uniqueness of the descent involution at each tower level; the fixed point of the brane recursion forces this involutive splitting. One then exhibits the eigenspace decomposition A_n = A_n^+ \oplus A_n^- and identifies the +-eigenspace as the physical part of the algebra—the part that survives the classical limit and feeds the mass observables. Finally, one assembles these per-level decompositions into the mass-decomposition formula. The next section's cosimplicial machinery promotes this formula into a genuine higher-categorical structure.
